X.note: Almost pitch black. Untextured blocky buildings, cannon and shot are black blobs, no people. Reads as a low-poly game blockout. The flag is the only readable element.

Y.note: Same blockout as X with slightly lifted ground and a warm window glow. The buildings are still smooth, plain boxes and the ground is a flat brown plane. There are no people and nothing is happening, so it looks unfinished.

Z.note: Same scene, but with weathered plaster, rubble, barrels, a wagon, wheel ruts, a lantern glow and redcoat figures. It is moody and believable as a bombarded garrison at night. Figures are tiny and dark, and the lighting is still very dim, but it is by far the most convincing.

why: Z has real surface texture, props and human activity that sell a besieged 1782 garrison, while X is a near-black, untextured blockout with nothing legible.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with the 1801 St Patrick's cross (the 1606 flag had only two crosses) in all frames
Buildings are too plain and clean in X/Y for a battered siege-era town
